events.content: Create a single-file HTML page (index.html) with all CSS and JavaScript inline and zero external assets. Render a dark, atmospheric hero scene featuring a single, steaming bowl of vegan ramen as the sole visual focus. Make the dish feel alive and appetizing — with natural motion, ambient warmth, and interactive response to the mouse. Keep the scene pure (no UI, text, or menus), responsive on all screens, and respectful of prefers-reduced-motion.

I’ll build this as a self-contained procedural canvas scene, so the bowl, broth, toppings, steam, glow, and interaction remain crisp and responsive without external assets. I’ll first inspect the workspace, then implement and verify the single-file page.

The workspace is empty, so I’m creating `index.html` from scratch. The composition will use layered canvas drawing: a charcoal dining surface, a warm ceramic bowl, reflective broth, hand-drawn vegan toppings, subtle broth ripples, and steam that bends gently toward the pointer. Reduced-motion mode will render the same scene statically while preserving pointer-based lighting.

The page is implemented and the inline script parses cleanly with no `src` or `href` dependencies. I’m doing a headless browser render now to catch any runtime or visual-composition issues—especially clipping, layering, and small-screen scaling.

The desktop render is balanced and atmospheric. The mobile check also works, but the bowl reads slightly too small on a narrow portrait viewport, so I’m tightening that responsive scale to keep the ramen unmistakably dominant without cropping the steam or ceramic body.
The responsive adjustment is in. I’m running the final static/reduced-motion checks now; after that I’ll do the session’s required Dawnmark inbox check before handing the file back.

Created [index.html](<WORKSPACE>/openai/gpt-5.6-sol/high/index.html).

It features:

- Procedurally drawn vegan ramen with tofu, mushrooms, bok choy, noodles, scallions, chili oil, and nori
- Animated steam and broth ripples
- Mouse-responsive lighting, parallax, and steam direction
- Responsive desktop and mobile composition
- Static rendering for `prefers-reduced-motion`
- All CSS and JavaScript inline, with zero external assets

Validated in Chromium at desktop, mobile, and reduced-motion settings.

excluded: large base64 and embedded image data (event retained with size marker)
